newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares jump as political impasse ends.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares jump as political impasse ends.

text.p: Slovenian shares bounced higher on Friday as the market welcomed the approval of a new government and on hopes that the end to the political impasse may encourage foreign investors to return.
The new government was voted in late on Thursday after Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek's first cabinet proposal was voted down.
"I think the time of extensive foreign buying is approaching," said Gregor Pajic, a trader at brokerage Certius.
"I expect foreign buyers to return to our market in the near-future. The serious long-term international investors were never scared by costs of custody accounts," he added.
The central bank earlier this month ordered foreign investors to open special custody accounts at one of Slovenia's 14 fully licenced banks in order to trade in country's securities.
The bourse plummeted on the news but the central bank later defended its move as regulating foreign portfolio investment -- not blocking it.
The SBI index rose 35.38 points to 1,431.06. The blue-chip index has risen 5.07 percent over the last two days.
Market turnover jumped to 386.2 million tolars from 136.8 million. Overall 15 shares rose, one fell and 10 were untraded.
Drug maker Lek's A issue was the most actively traded share, firming 1.57 percent to an average price of 28,401 tolars on volume of 7,736 shares for total turnover of 219.7 million tolars.
Brokerage Finmedia was the biggest gainer, surging 9.93 percent to 13,700 tolars on volume of one share.
Brokerage Primofin was the only decliner, tumbling 9.01 percent to 12,102 tolars on volume of 89 shares.
